- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–2% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30), model frequently overestimates; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias unless sentiment is strong positive (>0.30).
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >1.5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates when sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment if sentiment variance >0.30 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is rising, model may misread trend; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for each day sentiment < -0.30.
